```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Here, we parse the output of the script.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
setwd(here::here("output"))

method <- "umap" # tsne or umap
input <- paste0(method, "_runs_100_cells_10000_scale_nozscore.rds")
dimr_list <- readr::read_rds(input)

# Tidy
dimr_list <- lapply(dimr_list, function(i) {
    names(i) <- c("dimr1", "dimr2")
    return(i)
})
```
```{r}
cell_id <- 1
one_cell <- lapply(dimr_list, function(i) {
    return(i[cell_id,])
}) %>% bind_rows()

ggplot(one_cell, aes(x = dimr1, y = dimr2)) + geom_point(size = 5)
```

Now we need to view each of the UMAP conformations.

```{r}
ggplot(dimr_list[[1]], aes(x = dimr1, y = dimr2)) + geom_point()
ggplot(dimr_list[[3]], aes(x = dimr1, y = dimr2)) + geom_point()
```

Ok, so it's indeed two very distinct conformations. But we need to see the full gif. And we need to create the animation directly in R.

```{r}
all_data <- bind_rows(dimr_list) # dplyr's bind_rows is convenient

# Determine limits with a little padding
xlims <- range(all_data[[1]]) + c(-0.5, 0.5)
ylims <- range(all_data[[2]]) + c(-0.5, 0.5)
```

```{r}
library(magick)
library(animation)
setwd(here::here("output"))

# Define the output filename for the GIF
gif_file <- paste0(method, "_animation.gif")

# Set options for the animation package
# You might need to specify the path to the 'magick' executable
# if `animation` can't find it automatically, e.g.:
# ani.options(convert = 'C:/Program Files/ImageMagick-7.1.0-Q16-HDRI/magick.exe')
# Often, simply having the 'magick' R package installed is sufficient.
# Check ani.options("convert")
toplot <- lapply(dimr_list, function(i) {
    color <- rep("other", nrow(i))
    color[cell_id] <- "highlight"
    result <- bind_cols(i, highlight_point = color)
    return(result)
})

# Use saveGIF to create the animation
saveGIF({
    # Loop through each UMAP tibble in the list
    for (i in seq_along(toplot)) {
        # Get the current UMAP data
        current_dimr <- toplot[[i]]

        # Create the ggplot object for the current frame
        p <- ggplot(current_dimr, aes(x = dimr1, y = dimr2)) +
            geom_point(data = subset(current_dimr, highlight_point == "other"),
                  color = "black", size = 1.5) +
            # Then, add the highlighted point on top
            geom_point(data = subset(current_dimr, highlight_point == "highlight"), color = "yellow", size = 10) +
            coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = xlims, ylim = ylims) + # Ensures consistent axes
            theme_minimal() +
            labs(
                title = paste("Frame:", i),
                x = "dimr 1",
                y = "dimr 2"
            ) +
             theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) # Center title

        # IMPORTANT: Print the plot object so saveGIF captures it
        print(p)
    }
},
    movie.name = gif_file,   # Name of the output GIF file
    interval = 0.3,          # Time interval between frames (in seconds)
    ani.width = 600,         # Width of the GIF in pixels
    ani.height = 600         # Height of the GIF in pixels
)
```

```{r}
setwd(here::here("output"))

# Check if the GIF file was created
if (file.exists(gif_file)) {
    # Read the GIF using the magick package
    dimr_gif <- image_read(gif_file)

    # Print the magick object - this should display it in RStudio's Viewer
    # or potentially the Plots pane depending on your setup.
    print(dimr_gif)

    # Optional: Get info about the GIF
    # print(image_info(umap_gif))

} else {
    warning("GIF file was not created successfully.")
}

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("output", gif_file))
```
